title: Redact before publication
text:
Derive the public boundary from the data
An internal event can carry information that a public consumer must never receive. Suppose event 1 has public code 7 and sensitive value 424242. The public consumer needs the identifier and code. Removing the sensitive value before that consumer runs is a property of the whole path from producer to consumer, including the values seen by intermediate callbacks.
The hook pipeline showed how each callback receives the preceding stage’s result. The hook lesson established that every callback preserves the hook’s payload type. Those two facts give us separate jobs: choose which internal stages can inspect the sensitive field, then construct a public value before crossing the public interface.
Represent the internal event by three integers: identifier, public code, and secret, in that order. A public event has only the first two. The intended calculation is non-executable notation:
These operations answer different questions. Redaction preserves the internal shape so it can participate in an internal hook. Projection — choosing a subset of fields to form the new value — changes the shape so the secret field has no position in the public result. Both operations must preserve the identifier and code. We also assume those two input fields are suitable for publication; a type with two integers cannot establish that policy.
Work backward from the consumer. Give collect_public input type PublicEvent; it returns that value as the observation collected here. Then public_view : InternalEvent -> PublicEvent supplies exactly its input. Separate InternalFeed and PublicFeed hooks preserve their own payloads. CollectInternal.capture instead requests an ordinary snapshot collection; it is an effect operation interpreted by our surrounding handler.
Keep these definitions in events.ash:
The module rules make the exported types, constructors, functions, and effects available through an importing alias. pub controls that access; it does not classify data as confidential. InternalEvent and PublicEvent are distinct nominal types, and the public constructor deliberately remains available. This lets us examine what the chosen interface actually guarantees.
public_view selects the first two fields and constructs a different type. redact constructs another internal event with secret 0. Neither can change the original event saved by an earlier snapshot. Each calculation inspects three fields and constructs one fixed-size value; its source-level work is constant in this representation.
Enter redacting-before-publication/src from the Cases directory. In 01-public-view.ash, projection happens before public publication:
Predict the exact public event. Its identifier and code should be unchanged, with no third field:
The ordinary collector is also a valid public callback because its type is PublicEvent -> PublicEvent. It returns the value it receives. The public hook never carries an internal event. The hook contract checks these connections; the equation for public_view explains why these particular public fields are the intended ones.

title: Redact before publication
section: Two rejected connections and their repairs
text:
Two rejected connections and their repairs
Could projection itself be an internal transformation? Try registering public_view in 06-type-changing-registration.ash:
import events as Events

main : Unit -> Events.InternalEvent
main () = hook Events.InternalFeed {
    register Events.InternalFeed Events.public_view {
        perform Events.InternalFeed.publish (Events.InternalEvent(1, 7, 424242))
    }
}
The target’s payload is InternalEvent, so the callback must accept and return that type. Predict which end of public_view fails that requirement. Run from the same src directory:
$ ash --message-format human --locale en 06-type-changing-registration.ash
This expression must have type `InternalEvent -> InternalEvent`, but it has type `InternalEvent -> PublicEvent`.
  --> /path/to/ash-doc/content/cases/redacting-before-publication/src/06-type-changing-registration.ash:5:5
5 |     register Events.InternalFeed Events.public_view {
  |     ^ This has type `InternalEvent -> PublicEvent`.
6 |         perform Events.InternalFeed.publish (Events.InternalEvent(1, 7, 424242))
  | ^ This has type `InternalEvent -> PublicEvent`.
7 |     }
  | ^ This has type `InternalEvent -> PublicEvent`.
reason: type.mismatch
The message compares InternalEvent -> InternalEvent, required by the registration, with InternalEvent -> PublicEvent, supplied by public_view. Its label spans the registration and its body, where that callback contract is imposed. The input agrees; the result does not. Both feed declarations qualify as hooks, so this is an ordinary type mismatch, reported secondarily as type.mismatch.
The repair is the complete program 01-public-view.ash: project the internal value before publishing on PublicFeed, and register collect_public, whose input and result are both PublicEvent. Changing just the hook name while keeping public_view as callback would still leave its input type wrong. The repaired program returns the public event already observed above.
The consumer’s input boundary can reject an internal value even without a hook. 07-internal-to-public.ash attempts that connection directly:
import events as Events

main : Unit -> Events.PublicEvent
main () = Events.collect_public (Events.InternalEvent(1, 7, 424242))
$ ash --message-format human --locale en 07-internal-to-public.ash
This function argument must have type `PublicEvent`, but has type `InternalEvent`.
  --> /path/to/ash-doc/content/cases/redacting-before-publication/src/07-internal-to-public.ash:4:33
4 | main () = Events.collect_public (Events.InternalEvent(1, 7, 424242))
  |                                 ^ This has type `InternalEvent`.
  --> /path/to/ash-doc/content/cases/redacting-before-publication/src/events.ash:28:5
28 | pub collect_public : PublicEvent -> PublicEvent
   |     ^ This function requires an argument of type `PublicEvent`.
  --> /path/to/ash-doc/content/cases/redacting-before-publication/src/07-internal-to-public.ash:4:11
4 | main () = Events.collect_public (Events.InternalEvent(1, 7, 424242))
  |           ^ This is the containing function application.
reason: type.argument
The first label identifies the supplied InternalEvent. The label in events.ash points to collect_public, whose declared domain requires PublicEvent; the final label locates the containing application. These three labels connect the rejected argument to the consumer contract. The secondary identifier is type.argument.
For this second repair, replace the argument with the explicit projection. The following replacement expression is a non-executable fragment, to use as the body of main in a scratch copy of the preceding program:
Events.collect_public (Events.public_view (Events.InternalEvent(1, 7, 424242)))
Run the repaired copy. It produces the same PublicEvent(1, 7) as the public pipeline. The two repairs enforce the intended connection at different places: the public hook carries only public values, and the ordinary consumer accepts only public values. Diagnostic wording and source layout describe this tool’s presentation; the nominal type and callback requirements are the language boundary.

Practice: choose the observation boundary

title: Check proposed edits
text:
Keep the original outside the proposal
A worker can propose a plausible result without having permission to make its changes. A controller needs more than a finished list: it needs the proposed edits, the original list it trusts, and the positions the worker may change. It can then reconstruct the expected result before allowing the worker to complete.
The scripted session separated a calculation from the commands supplied by its handler. Here one immutable proposal contains an entire edit batch and its candidate artifact. Continue from resumption and early stopping: resuming a worker safely and approving its data are separate responsibilities.
Use a finite list of integers as the artifact. Positions start at zero. The controller owns original [10,20,30] and allowed positions [1,2]. A worker proposes 1 := 25, then 2 := 35, together with candidate [10,25,35]. Square brackets and := here are non-executable notation; the Ash data below uses constructors.
The proposal contains an edits list and one candidate. It contains neither an authoritative original nor an authoritative permission list. That keeps the question precise: does this proposed artifact result from these edits to our original, and is each requested position permitted? Reviewing an entire immutable batch also avoids a changing current artifact between review rounds. A session with several rounds would need an additional agreement about that current state.
Derive the operation contracts from the desired result. make_proposal receives an original and edits and constructs their candidate. Review.propose takes the proposal and requests a Decision. Allow lets the worker return Completed(candidate); Reject(reason) lets it return Rejected(reason). A controller that stops the waiting worker instead constructs Cancelled. Those constructors are ordinary data; their names confer no permission.
The controller must establish three conditions before allowing the batch:
Existence comes first so position 7 is missing, while existing position 0 is forbidden. A write of 0 := 10 is still forbidden even though it would leave that field unchanged. Permission is about the proposed operation, not only the difference between final artifacts.

title: Check proposed edits
section: Observe three ways to finish review
text:
Observe three ways to finish review
Enter checking-proposed-edits/src from the Cases directory. The three entries share the original, batch, worker, and controller. Only their script choice changes. Predict both the ordinary result and whether the worker’s post-request marker is reached.
import edits as Edits
import controller as Controller

main : Unit -> (Edits.Result, Bool)
main () = Controller.run Controller.Check
$ ash 01-allow.ash
(Completed(Item(10, Item(25, Item(35, End)))), true) : (Result, Bool)
All validation conditions pass, so the clause resumes with Allow. The worker reaches its marker and returns the candidate [10,25,35]. The true records that resumed suffix, not a separate claim that the artifact is correct.
import edits as Edits
import controller as Controller

main : Unit -> (Edits.Result, Bool)
main () = Controller.run Controller.Refuse
$ ash 02-reject.ash
(Rejected(ScriptedRejection), true) : (Result, Bool)
Refuse resumes with Reject(ScriptedRejection). The worker still continues after the request, reaches the marker, and returns Rejected with that reason. Rejecting the proposal is an ordinary answer to the operation.
import edits as Edits
import controller as Controller

main : Unit -> (Edits.Result, Bool)
main () = Controller.run Controller.Cancel
$ ash 03-cancel.ash
(Cancelled, false) : (Result, Bool)
Cancel supplies no operation answer. Discard consumes the continuation that would have reached the marker and interpreted the decision. The clause then returns Cancelled, leaving the marker false. This local capture owns no resource or cleanup obligation; the accepted discard does not establish that an arbitrary suspended worker can always be abandoned safely.

title: Cancel a stable sort
text:
Choose the records and the complete result
A comparison budget can stop a sort before it has an answer. That creates two separate promises: a completed result must put records in the intended order, and a cancelled result must report only the comparison work already allowed. Calling an unfinished sequence sorted would hide the distinction.
Continue from ordered tree search, measuring comparisons, and bounded search. Those Cases separated an ordering invariant, a named unit of work, and a handler that can stop further work. Here the algorithm also preserves the input order of equal-priority records. That property is called stability.
A record has a priority and an identifier. Choose three priorities, ordered Low, then Normal, then High. This is our application’s relation, defined by the comparator below; constructor declaration order supplies no such rule. Identifiers let us recognize records and the original order of ties. They do not participate in comparison.
Use this input, with slash notation meaning priority and identifier:
The intended result is Low/2, Low/5, Normal/1, Normal/3, High/4. Low records retain input IDs 2,5; Normal records retain 1,3. Preserving every complete record is a separate requirement from putting its priority in order. A result that lost one Low record could be ordered without being a permutation of the input.
Derive two interfaces from complete versus cancelled work. Sorting returns Records; only finishing that calculation allows its caller to construct Sorted(records). A handler that abandons it returns Cancelled instead. Before comparing two records, insertion requests Compare.allow : Unit -> Unit. An answer lets that comparison run; discard abandons the pending comparison and the waiting Sorted construction.
We will return a triple: result, used comparison count, and a comparison trace. The count belongs to the permission policy. The trace records operand IDs and the ordering actually returned by the comparator. Keeping both observations will show whether denied permission accidentally ran a comparison.

title: Cancel a stable sort
text:
Calculate the seven comparisons
Before running, work from the end of the input toward its beginning. Inserting Low/5 into empty needs no comparison. High/4 passes Low/5. Normal/3 passes Low/5 and stops before High/4. Low/2 stops before equal Low/5. Finally, Normal/1 passes the two Low records and stops before equal Normal/3. The count is 0 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 3 = 7.

Check the result against an independent pure calculation. reference.ash filters the input separately for Low, Normal, and High, preserving order in each pass, then concatenates those three groups. It shares the record representation but uses neither insertion nor the comparator:
import sort as Sort

keep_low : Sort.Records -> Sort.Records
keep_low Sort.End = Sort.End
keep_low (Sort.More(record, rest)) = {
    let Sort.Record(priority, ignored_id) = record
    match priority {
        Sort.Low => Sort.More(record, keep_low rest)
        other => keep_low rest
    }
}

keep_normal : Sort.Records -> Sort.Records
keep_normal Sort.End = Sort.End
keep_normal (Sort.More(record, rest)) = {
    let Sort.Record(priority, ignored_id) = record
    match priority {
        Sort.Normal => Sort.More(record, keep_normal rest)
        other => keep_normal rest
    }
}

keep_high : Sort.Records -> Sort.Records
keep_high Sort.End = Sort.End
keep_high (Sort.More(record, rest)) = {
    let Sort.Record(priority, ignored_id) = record
    match priority {
        Sort.High => Sort.More(record, keep_high rest)
        other => keep_high rest
    }
}

append : (Sort.Records, Sort.Records) -> Sort.Records
append (Sort.End, right) = right
append (Sort.More(record, rest), right) = Sort.More (
    record, append (rest, right)
)

pub grouped : Sort.Records -> Sort.Records
grouped records = append (
    keep_low records, append (keep_normal records, keep_high records)
)
Each filter retains an entire selected record before filtering the rest, so it preserves the selected records’ input order. The three constructors cover all priorities exactly once across the filters. Concatenating the groups in the chosen order therefore supplies an independent stable reference for this finite priority domain.

title: Cancel a stable sort
section: Bound source work after naming its unit
text:
Bound source work after naming its unit
The seven calls describe one finite input. To obtain a general bound, let an insertion receive an ordered tail of length m. It makes at most m comparisons and reconstructs the passed prefix. The stopping case constructs both More(record, ...) and the current list node; reaching empty constructs one node. Altogether one insertion constructs at most m + 1 list nodes.
Sorting n records inserts into tails of lengths 0 through n - 1. Consequently, comparisons are bounded by n(n - 1)/2 and cumulative newly constructed record-list nodes by n(n + 1)/2. The original nodes and unused tails are immutable; these allocation counts do not describe peak live memory or physical stack use. The trace adds one observation node per comparison.
Three possible priorities still permit quadratic work. Consider k High records followed by k Low records. Sorting the Low block keeps it together. Each earlier High must pass all k Low records before reaching the High group or the end. Those crossings alone contribute k * k comparisons and prefix reconstruction. This is a source-work argument using comparisons and constructor operations as units; it is not a timing benchmark or a claim about evaluator handler search and physical representation costs.
Insertion keeps its equality position and charge point visible. A merge sort would offer a different work bound, but would need separate splitting, merging, and tie-order arguments. The present algorithm answers this smaller question with those two decisions next to each other.

Both completed results contain the same complete records shown above. At six, the next comparison would be Normal/1 against Normal/3. The handler denies its permission request, so that seventh call is absent and the result is Cancelled. At seven, that call runs and insertion completes without another request. A larger budget does not force an extra comparison.
Cancellation reports earlier allowed work without returning a partial sequence. Discard does not undo the counter writes or earlier trace entries. The selected continuation contains pending insertion work and the final Sorted construction; abandoning it prevents both from finishing. These are synchronous permission points in this calculation, not asynchronous interrupts.
Small inputs check the boundary where no comparison is needed, and three identical priorities make the stability condition visible:
import sort as Sort

main : Unit -> (
    (Sort.Result, Int, Sort.Comparisons),
    (Sort.Result, Int, Sort.Comparisons),
    (Sort.Result, Int, Sort.Comparisons)
)
main () = (
    Sort.run (Sort.End, 0),
    Sort.run (Sort.More(Sort.Record(Sort.High, 9), Sort.End), 0),
    Sort.run (Sort.equals (), 2)
)
$ ash 03-small-inputs.ash
((Sorted(End), 0, Done), (Sorted(More(Record(High, 9), End)), 0, Done), (Sorted(More(Record(Normal, 11), More(Record(Normal, 12), More(Record(Normal, 13), End)))), 2, Comparison(12, 13, Same, Comparison(11, 12, Same, Done)))) : ((Result, Int, Comparisons), (Result, Int, Comparisons), (Result, Int, Comparisons))

title: Round-trip a tagged frame
text:
Derive the format from its messages
An encoder and a decoder can agree with each other while both use the wrong format. A second boundary can hide the mistake: a buffer may have room for more bytes than the input actually contains. A decoder that treats unwritten, zeroed storage as input could invent a missing field or report trailing data that was never supplied.
Continue from bounded messages, buffer acquisition, and scoped access. Here we will check one small format independently in both directions, keep logical input length separate from capacity, and return only ordinary decoded data after buffer access ends.
A Ping has no fields. A Reading has one integer field, and a Pair has two ordered integer fields. Give each constructor a tag, then write its fields in order. The whole input must contain exactly one frame:
Square brackets in this chapter are non-executable list notation. The Ash programs represent these sequences as Byte(value, rest) ending in End. The name ByteValues denotes this ordinary list of integers. It is not the primitive immutable byte type, and its element type does not establish a byte range. Admitted payload fields must be in 0..255; checked native writes will enforce that condition.
Keep the ordinary data in frames.ash:
Next distinguishes a supplied integer from logical end of frame. End is not a special byte value: zero is meaningful as both a tag and a payload. The decoder returns Decoded(message) only after reading all expected fields and confirming that no supplied byte remains. An unknown tag gives BadTag, a missing tag or field gives Truncated, and extra input after a complete message gives TrailingData.
These are application results. Buffer acquisition and operations have their own outcome family, declared by the source buffer library. Derive the public operation as non-executable contract notation:
The outer outcome answers whether acquisition succeeded and its body returned normally. The inner outcome is the body’s checked-operation result. For example, Success(Success(Truncated)) means the buffer and operations succeeded but the supplied frame was incomplete. Success(Failure(InvalidIndex)) means acquisition succeeded but an operation failed. Keep both layers even though they use the same constructors.

title: Round-trip a tagged frame
section: Check both directions before relying on a round trip
text:
Check both directions before relying on a round trip
Use distinct pair fields so a reversal cannot pass unnoticed. The five hand-calculated goldens are Ping, Reading(0), Reading(255), Pair(0,255), and Pair(255,0). In 01-round-trips.ash, the first result group encodes those messages. The second decodes independent literal golden lists. Only the third feeds the encoder’s results into the decoder.
import @ffi.native_buffer as Buffer
import frames as Frames
import codec as Codec

type FrameInputs = NoFrames
    | Frame(Int, Frames.ByteValues, FrameInputs)
type Checks = Done
    | Checked(Buffer.Outcome<Buffer.Outcome<Frames.DecodeResult>>, Checks)

check_frames : FrameInputs -> Checks
check_frames NoFrames = Done
check_frames (Frame(capacity, byte_values, rest)) = Checked (
    Codec.run_frame (capacity, byte_values), check_frames rest
)

main : Unit -> (
    (Frames.ByteValues, Frames.ByteValues, Frames.ByteValues, Frames.ByteValues, Frames.ByteValues),
    Checks,
    Checks
)
main () = {
    let ping = Frames.Byte(0, Frames.End)
    let reading_zero = Frames.Byte(1, Frames.Byte(0, Frames.End))
    let reading_max = Frames.Byte(1, Frames.Byte(255, Frames.End))
    let pair_forward = Frames.Byte(2, Frames.Byte(0, Frames.Byte(255, Frames.End)))
    let pair_reverse = Frames.Byte(2, Frames.Byte(255, Frames.Byte(0, Frames.End)))
    let golden_frames = Frame (1, ping,
        Frame (2, reading_zero,
            Frame (2, reading_max,
                Frame (3, pair_forward, Frame (3, pair_reverse, NoFrames)))))
    let encoded_frames = Frame (1, Codec.encode Frames.Ping,
        Frame (2, Codec.encode (Frames.Reading 0),
            Frame (2, Codec.encode (Frames.Reading 255),
                Frame (3, Codec.encode (Frames.Pair(0, 255)),
                    Frame (3, Codec.encode (Frames.Pair(255, 0)), NoFrames)))))
    (
        (
            Codec.encode Frames.Ping,
            Codec.encode (Frames.Reading 0),
            Codec.encode (Frames.Reading 255),
            Codec.encode (Frames.Pair(0, 255)),
            Codec.encode (Frames.Pair(255, 0))
        ),
        check_frames golden_frames,
        check_frames encoded_frames
    )
}

section: Find logical end before looking at spare storage
text:
Find logical end before looking at spare storage
Use the same build/run pair with 02-malformed.ash. Predict which inputs supply a complete frame, which omit required input, and which supply too much:
import @ffi.native_buffer as Buffer
import frames as Frames
import codec as Codec

type FrameInputs = NoFrames
    | Frame(Int, Frames.ByteValues, FrameInputs)
type Checks = Done
    | Checked(Buffer.Outcome<Buffer.Outcome<Frames.DecodeResult>>, Checks)

check_frames : FrameInputs -> Checks
check_frames NoFrames = Done
check_frames (Frame(capacity, byte_values, rest)) = Checked (
    Codec.run_frame (capacity, byte_values), check_frames rest
)

main : Unit -> Checks
main () = {
    let inputs = Frame (1, Frames.Byte(9, Frames.End),
        Frame (1, Frames.Byte(1, Frames.End),
            Frame (2, Frames.Byte(2, Frames.Byte(7, Frames.End)),
                Frame (2, Frames.Byte(0, Frames.Byte(9, Frames.End)),
                    Frame (1, Frames.End,
                        Frame (2, Frames.Byte(1, Frames.End),
                            Frame (3, Frames.Byte(0, Frames.End), NoFrames)))))))
    check_frames inputs
}
The generated program returns seven nested outcomes, grouped by Checked and Done. The table lists the supplied inputs in source order:

These seven complete outcomes are selected from that one captured result in the same order, with the surrounding Checked and Done grouping omitted:
Success(Success(BadTag))
Success(Success(Truncated))
Success(Success(Truncated))
Success(Success(TrailingData))
Success(Success(Truncated))
Success(Success(Truncated))
Success(Success(Decoded(Ping)))
Tag 9 names no case. Tag 1 needs one field, and tag 2 needs two, so the next two inputs are truncated. Ping needs no payload, making the supplied 9 in [0,9] trailing data.
The final three cases distinguish input from storage. Empty input reaches logical end immediately, even though capacity is one. A lone Reading tag is still truncated at capacity two: the unwritten zero at index one is not its payload. Conversely, [0] is a valid Ping at capacity three: spare zeroed storage is not trailing input. Both outcomes follow from list-derived logical length, without reading those unused bytes.

Make scratch copies outside this lesson’s src directory. Keep frames.ash and codec.ash beside the entries that import them. Predict each result, then build and run with the same native root and cache settings.

Change the Pair tag in the encoder only. Explain which independent golden check and which round-trip observation can distinguish the change.

In a scratch cursor closure, perform the read before returning the function and capture only the copied integer. Explain which owner is still needed.

Golden bytes establish the chosen format, logical length establishes which input belongs to the frame, and scoped access establishes where buffer operations may run. A round trip connects those boundaries only when its payload and successful-operation premises hold. A larger format would next need an explicit policy for framing several messages or reporting where a failed parse stopped; those are additional questions to design separately.
